value.text:
The Conservatoire national supérieur de musique et de danse de Lyon (CNSMDL) is a French public higher education institution specialising in professional music and dance training in Lyon. It has the status of an établissement public à caractère administratif under the supervision of the Ministry of Culture and is an associate member of the Université de Lyon. Admission to its professional programmes is by competitive examination.

Teaching began in October 1979 with 46 students, before the Conservatoire national supérieur de musique de Lyon was formally created by decree on 18 February 1980. The dance department was established in January 1984. The institution moved into renovated premises at the Clos des Deux-Amants in 1988; dance studios at the Grenier d’abondance opened in June 1993. Dance was officially added to its institutional name in February 2009.

Its programmes cover musical and dance performance, musical creation, musical culture and pedagogy. The French account describes three study cycles, including national professional diplomas, qualifications carrying master grade and artist diplomas. Partner institutions award the associated licence and doctorate qualifications. The Clos des Deux-Amants houses music teaching rooms, performance spaces and the Nadia-Boulanger media library. In 2020, the conservatoire reported 643 students, 189 teaching staff and 69 administrative staff, with a budget of €15 million.
